title: AI assistance log — PQHS 431 Lab 5
text:
AI assistance log — PQHS 431 Lab 5
Tool: ChatGPT (OpenAI)
Relevant user prompts from this work session (verbatim): - “Can I use the template of previous labs?” - “update my CV first” - “December 2023” - “ok update the cv” - “ok go a head”
Additional context: The user supplied screenshots of Emma Chio’s website as a visual reference and an existing CV. ChatGPT drafted Quarto website files (_quarto.yml, .qmd pages, CSS, SVG illustration), included the updated public CV PDF, and provided setup/publishing guidance. The website layout is inspired by the screenshots but the text and code were drafted anew. This log should be supplemented with the complete exact prompts used in future AI-assisted edits. For a fully precise disclosure, also include any earlier relevant prompts and the CV-editing prompts from the conversation history.

“Use my nursing honor society photo as the homepage profile picture.” — ChatGPT replaced the homepage illustration with the user-supplied nursing honor society photo and adjusted CSS for circular cropping.

title: Selected Projects
section: County-Level Health Patterns Across Six U.S. States
text:
County-Level Health Patterns Across Six U.S. States
PQHS 431 · Statistical Methods I
Analyzed county-level health measures using R and Quarto. Explored differences in life expectancy across states and changes in low birth weight rates, using visualizations and confidence intervals to communicate results.

title: Selected Projects
text:
AI in Medicine — Text Classification
PQHS 416 · AI in Medicine
Worked on a text classification project using the Reuters dataset, evaluating model performance and exploring the effects of different dropout settings.

title: Selected Projects
section: Geographic Information Systems for Public Health
text:
Geographic Information Systems for Public Health
PQHS 426 · GIS
Created maps and spatial analyses related to public health and neighborhood-level patterns, using geographic data to communicate complex relationships.

title: Selected Projects
text:
Evidence-Based Nursing Practice

Project descriptions summarize coursework and do not imply publication or independent clinical implementation.

title: Welcome
text:
Ali Almadan
Graduate Student in Biomedical & Health Informatics · Registered Nurse
I am a graduate student in Biomedical and Health Informatics at Case Western Reserve University. My background in nursing has shaped my interest in how data, technology, and research can help improve patient care and public health.
My academic interests include health data analysis, epidemiology, artificial intelligence in medicine, and geographic information systems. I enjoy learning how to turn complex health information into meaningful insights.
